facts.text: The Constitution of India has created the Parliament of India.
facts.quote: The Constitution of India has created the Parliament of India.

facts.text: The Legislature at the national level is called the Parliament; it consists of the President and two Houses, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
facts.quote: The Legislature at the national level, that is the level of the central government, is called the Parliament. It consists of the President and the two Houses of Parliament - Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

facts.text: The President is an inseparable part of the Parliament but cannot participate in the discussions in either House.
facts.quote: Though President is an inseparable part of the Parliament, he/she cannot participate in the discussions in either of the houses of the Parliament.

facts.text: The Lok Sabha is the lower and first house; as the House of Representatives directly elected by the people, it is called the 'First' house.
facts.quote: The Lok Sabha is the lower and the first house of the Parliament of India. Lok Sabha is the House of Representatives directly elected by the people. Hence, the Lok Sabha is called the 'First' house.

facts.text: Members of the Lok Sabha are elected directly by the people from 'territorial constituencies'.
facts.quote: The members of Lok Sabha are elected directly by people from the 'territorial constituencies'.

facts.text: The tenure of the Lok Sabha is five years; the elections held every five years are known as General Elections.
facts.quote: The tenure of Lok Sabha is five years. The elections take place after every five years. These elections are known as General Elections.

facts.text: When the Lok Sabha is dissolved before completing five years, the elections held are called mid-term elections.
facts.quote: However, there are examples when the Lok Sabha was dissolved before the completion of five years. Elections held in such a case are called mid-term elections.

facts.text: As per the constitution there can be a maximum of 552 members in the Lok Sabha.
facts.quote: As per the constitution there can be a maximum of 552 members in the Lok Sabha.

facts.text: Some Lok Sabha seats are reserved for members belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
facts.quote: To ensure representation to all sections of the society, some seats are reserved for members belonging to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes.

facts.text: If there are no representatives from the Anglo-Indian community, the President can appoint two members from this community to the Lok Sabha.
facts.quote: In case there are no representatives from the Anglo- Indian community, the President can appoint two members from this community to the Lok Sabha.

facts.text: The Rajya Sabha is the upper and second house of Parliament; its members are indirectly elected.
facts.quote: The upper and the second house of Parliament is the Rajya Sabha. The members of Rajya Sabha are indirectly elected.

facts.text: The Rajya Sabha gives representation to 28 states and 9 Union territories; its members represent the constituent states.
facts.quote: The Rajya Sabha gives representation to 28 states and 9 Union territories in India. Thus, members of Rajya Sabha work as representatives of the constituent states.

facts.text: States get Lok Sabha seats on the basis of population; each State is divided into territorial constituencies of approximately equal population; Maharashtra has 48 seats.
facts.quote: The constituent States in India get seats on basis of their population. For the purpose of elections, the State is divided into territorial constituencies. The population of these territorial constituencies is approximately equal. ... Maharashtra : 48 seats

facts.text: The total membership of the Rajya Sabha is 250; 238 members are elected from the constituent states and Union Territories.
facts.quote: The total membership of Rajya Sabha is 250 members. Amongst them, 238 members are elected from the constituent states and Union Territories.

facts.text: States do not get equal representation in the Rajya Sabha; it is proportionate to the total population of each state.
facts.quote: All the constituent states do not get equal representation in the Rajya Sabha. It is proportionate to the total population of each of the state.

facts.text: The remaining 12 Rajya Sabha members are appointed by the President, usually distinguished personalities from literature, arts, science, sports and social work.
facts.quote: Remaining 12 members are appointed by the President. These members are usually experienced and distinguished personalities from the fields of literature, arts, science, sports and social work.

facts.text: Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected through the system of proportional representation.
facts.quote: The members of Rajya Sabha are elected through the system of proportional representation.

facts.text: The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved completely, hence it is called a permanent house.
facts.quote: Rajya Sabha is never dissolved completely hence it is called a permanent house.

facts.text: One-third of Rajya Sabha members, having completed their six-year tenure, retire every two years and an equal number are elected, so it functions continuously.
facts.quote: 1/3rd members of total members of Rajya Sabha who have completed their tenure of six years retire after every two years and equal number of new members get elected. Because the limited members of Rajya Sabha retire step by step, Rajya Sabha can function continuously.

facts.text: A person contesting Rajya Sabha elections must be an Indian citizen and must have completed 30 years of age.
facts.quote: Any person contesting for the elections of Rajya Sabha must be an Indian citizen and he must have completed 30 years of age.

facts.text: One can vote after attaining 18 years of age, but contesting Lok Sabha elections needs 25 completed years of age.
facts.quote: You can vote after you attain 18 years of age, but you cannot contest elections! ... for contesting Lok Sabha elections one needs to complete 25 years of age

facts.text: The Lok Sabha election can be contested from any constituency of any state.
facts.quote: the Lok Sabha election can be contested from any constituency of any state.

facts.text: Members of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha are known as Members of Parliament (MPs); they raise questions in Parliament for their constituencies and the Government allocates them development funds.
facts.quote: Members of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha are known as Member of Parliament (MPs). MPs try to resolve the queries and complaints of their constituencies by raising questions in the Parliament. Government allocates them funds to carry out development work in their respective constituencies.

facts.text: Formulation of laws (new laws, repealing outdated laws, changing laws) is the primary and important responsibility of the Parliament.
facts.quote: the Parliament has to formulate new laws. Also, outdated laws are repealed, necessary changes are made in some laws. ... the Parliament fulfills this primary and important responsibility.

facts.text: Certain out-of-date (obsolete) laws are abolished, for example the abolition of Privy purses.
facts.quote: Certain laws which become out-of-date (obsolete) are abolished. ... For example, abolition of Privy purses.

facts.text: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers are drawn from the Parliament, which sees that the Council of Ministers does not disregard it and functions under its supervision.
facts.quote: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers are drawn from the Parliament and Parliament exercises control over them. ... It is the responsibility of the Parliament to see that the Council of Ministers does not disregard the Parliament and functions under its supervision.

facts.text: The Parliament decides whether to make any amendment to the Constitution; the constitution amendment bill is considered an important bill.
facts.quote: The Parliament decides whether to make any amendment to the Indian Constitution. The constitution amendment bill is considered to be an important bill.

facts.text: Ways of amending: some provisions by simple majority, some by special majority (2/3rd), and a few by special majority plus consent from more than half of the constituent states.
facts.quote: (i) Few provisions in the Indian Constitution are amended by simple majority of the Parliament (ii) Some provisions require special majority (2/3rd) of the Parliament. (iii) Few other provisions are amended by special majority of the Parliament plus consent from more than half of the constituent states.

facts.text: In the very first meeting after Lok Sabha elections, members elect a 'Speaker' and 'Deputy Speaker' from amongst themselves.
facts.quote: In the very first meeting after the elections of Lok Sabha, the members of Lok Sabha elect a 'Speaker' and 'Deputy Speaker' from amongst themselves.

facts.text: The Lok Sabha functions under the guidance and control of the Speaker; the Lok Sabha represents the citizens and the Speaker represents the Lok Sabha.
facts.quote: Lok Sabha functions under the guidance and control of the speaker. Lok Sabha represents the citizen and the Speaker represents the Lok Sabha.

facts.text: The Speaker conducts the business of the House unbiasedly, takes care of members' rights and privileges, maintains decorum and dignity and interprets the rules of the house.
facts.quote: he/she has to conduct the business of the House in an unbiased manner. Lok Sabha members have some rights and privileges ... These are taken care of by the Speaker. Apart from this, the Speaker has to maintain the decorum and dignity of the house as well as interpret the rules of daily functioning of the house

facts.text: The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
facts.quote: The Vice President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

facts.text: The Rajya Sabha Chairman maintains discipline in the house, facilitates discussions and gives members a chance to speak.
facts.quote: The functions of Rajya Sabha Chairman also include maintaining the discipline in the house, facilitating discussions, giving members a chance to speak etc.

facts.text: A rough draft of the law prepared at the start of the law-making process is known as the draft proposal of the law or Bill.
facts.quote: A rough draft of the law is prepared initially. This draft or outline is known as draft proposal of the law or Bill of law.

facts.text: Two types of bills are primarily introduced in Parliament: Money Bill and Ordinary Bill.
facts.quote: There are two types of bills that are primarily introduced in House of the Parliament. (1) Money Bill (2) Ordinary Bill.

facts.text: First reading: the minister of the concerned department or a member presents the bill and briefly explains its nature.
facts.quote: The minister of the concerned department/ministry or member of the parliament presents the bill and briefly explains its nature while presenting it. This is called as 'first reading'.

facts.text: Bills related to finance (such as taxes) are 'Money Bills', introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha has limited powers over them.
facts.quote: Bills related to taxes are related to finance. Bills related to finance are considered as 'Money Bills' and such bills are introduced and passed in the Lok Sabha. Rajya Sabha has limited powers with respect to money bills.

facts.text: If the Rajya Sabha feels that, in the national interest, Parliament should make a law on a State List subject, it can pass a resolution to that effect.
facts.quote: If Rajya Sabha feels that as a matter of national interest, the Parliament should make a law on the subject in the State List it can pass a resolution to that effect.

facts.text: Second reading has two stages; in the first, the bill's objectives are discussed and it may be sent to a committee of the House, whose report has instructions and recommendations.
facts.quote: There are two stages of second reading. In the first stage, the objectives of the proposed Bill are discussed ... the bill is sent to a committee of the House. The committee report consisting of instructions and recommendations is sent to the House

facts.text: In the second phase of the second reading, the bill is discussed clause by clause, members suggest changes and voting is taken.
facts.quote: In this phase, the bill is discussed clause by clause. Members can suggest changes. After this, voting is taken in the house.

facts.text: Third reading: the bill is discussed briefly again and voted on; with the required majority it is passed by the House.
facts.quote: The bill is discussed briefly again during the third reading. Voting is taken for approving the Bill. If the bill gets an assent by the required majority, then the bill is considered as passed by the House.

facts.text: The bill goes through the same procedure in the other house; after approval by both houses it is sent for the President's assent.
facts.quote: The bill undergoes the same procedure even in the other house. After getting an approval by both the houses, the bill is further sent for assent by the President.

facts.text: If the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha differ over a bill, its future is decided in a joint meeting of both houses.
facts.quote: If there occurs a difference of opinion between Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha over a specific bill, the future of this bill is decided in a joint meeting of both the houses.

facts.text: After the final assent and signature of the President, the bill is converted into law.
facts.quote: After the final assent and signature of the President, the bill is converted into the law and the law is made.

facts.text: Every year in February, the Finance Minister presents the national Budget to the Lok Sabha.
facts.quote: Every year in the month of February, the Finance Minister presents the national Budget to the Lok Sabha.

facts.text: State Legislatures follow the same law-making procedure; a Bill passed by a State Legislature becomes a Law only after the assent of the Governor.
facts.quote: The State Legislatures also follow the same procedure of law making as in the Parliament. The Bill passed by the State Legislature can become a Law only after it receives the assent of the Governor.
